replies.What is your relationship with mathemati: Mathematics has always felt distant to me. I prefer art and literature subjects. Numbers and formulas seem abstract and cold. I learned some basics in school but never really engaged deeply. It's more about creativity for me, not calculation.
replies.Do you ever get anxious when thinking ab: Honestly, not really. I'm not very neurotic about these things. If I had to try math, I'd probably feel a bit lost or frustrated but not anxious. I prefer visual arts and stories, so numbers just don't grab my attention emotionally.
replies.Did you ever use AI to support your math: No, I haven't. I never really needed to. My vocational training didn't require math. I've relied on intuition and creativity instead. I don't see why I'd want to use AI for something I'm not interested in or good at.
replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: I'd be honest I'm not great at this. But generally, you find the coefficients, apply the quadratic formula, and solve for the two roots. It involves factoring or using the discriminant. I'd need to study more to explain it well without mistakes.

To find stationary points, you take the derivative of the function. Then set it equal to zero. Solve for x. Those are the points where the slope is flat. It's calculus, which I've never done. My strength is in art and writing.
